knowledge_point.title: Integrating Products Containing Other Exponential Functions

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 - x^{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(- 4 x^{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 3 \cdot 2^{2 - x^{4}} x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{3}{4}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}+C.
$$

$$
- \frac{3}{4}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- \frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{2^{u}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- \frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{2^{2 - x^{4}}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)+C.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3^{x} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3^{x} \ln{\left(3 \right)})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Use a connected real interval on which the integrand is defined.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2 \cdot 3^{x}}{3^{x} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\ln\left|u\right|+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\left(\ln\left|u\right|\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}\left(\ln\left|3^{x} + 1\right|\right)+C.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=1 - x^{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(- 2 x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=1\\x=\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}&\Longrightarrow u=1 - \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\sqrt{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}} x e^{1 - x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{1}^{1 - \ln{\left(2 \right)}} e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Endpoint values: $e^{\ln 2}=2,\quad e^{2\ln 2}=4$.

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=e^{u}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
- \frac{1}{2}\left(\left[e^{u}\right]_{1}^{1 - \ln{\left(2 \right)}}\right)=- \frac{1}{2}\left(\left(\frac{e}{2}\right)-\left(e\right)\right).
$$

The exact answer is

$$
\frac{e}{4}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Sine

question.:question/problem:
Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{9}{4 \sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{9}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{9}{4 \sqrt{1 - 9 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{4}\left(\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arcsin{\left(3 x \right)}}{4}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{50 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(5)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
50 x^{2} + 2=2\left(1+(5 x)^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{5}=\frac{3}{10}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{50 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{10}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arctan{\left(5 x \right)}}{10}+C.
$$
